jobs.company: NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration
jobs.title: Environmental Protection Specialist (Direct Hire)
jobs.description:
Summary

Join NASA's Office of Strategic Infrastructure (OSI) as the JPL Site Environmental Technical Manager and help enable mission success through environmental stewardship and regulatory compliance. You will provide technical leadership for complex environmental programs supporting JPL's mission operations, infrastructure, construction, and facilities while ensuring compliance with federal environmental requirements.

Duties

Help

Serves as Environmental Technical Manager for JPL sites including the main Oak Grove campus in Pasadena, California, the Goldstone Deep Space Communication Complex in Fort Irwin, California and Table Mountain Facility in Wrightwood, California.
Serves as the civil servant signatory authority responsible for certifying regulatory JPL submittals to applicable environmental regulatory agencies.
Oversees National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) reviews and Section 106 consultations with Tribal Nations and State Historic Preservation Offices (SHPOs).
Leads environmental regulatory negotiations, permitting activities, coordination with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies, and related inherently governmental functions.
Develops, implements, and evaluates environmental compliance programs to ensure JPL operations meet applicable laws, regulations, policies, and permit requirements.
Provides authoritative technical guidance to NASA and JPL leadership and stakeholders on complex environmental issues, compliance risks, and requirements affecting mission execution.

Requirements

Help

Conditions of employment

This position is open to U.S. citizens, nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.
This position may require a one-year probationary period. If selected, the requirement to serve such period will be determined by Title 5 of the Code of Federal Regulations, Part 11. **See Additional Information section**
You must meet qualifications requirements by the closing date of this announcement.
Position subject to pre-employment background investigation or higher-level clearance. Investigation/Clearance may differ and be required based on the duty location/NASA Center requirements.
Financial Disclosure, Drug Testing, and/or the Travel Requirements for this position may differ and be required based on the duty location/NASA Center requirements.

Qualifications

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the particular ability, skill, and knowledge to successfully perform the duties of this position and is typically in or related to this line of work.

To qualify for GS-14
, you must have one year of directly related specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 level:

Providing technical leadership or oversight for complex environmental compliance programs;
Interpreting and applying federal environmental laws and regulations, such as NEPA, CERCLA, or Section 106 requirements;
Managing environmental permitting, reporting, regulatory coordination, or remediation activities;
Advising leadership on complex environmental compliance issues, risks, and requirements affecting facilities, infrastructure, or operations.
The following training is preferred but not required for this position: Resource Conservation and Recovery Act Information (RCRA) Hazardous Waste Generator Training, California Universal Waste Training (22 CCR 66273.36), RCRAInfo Training, DOT Hazmat Employee Training under 49 CFR 172.704, California Certified Emission Reductions (CERS) / Tier II Reporting Training

Your resume must include a clear and detailed narrative description, in your own words, of how you meet the required specialized experience. Experience statements copied from a position description, vacancy announcement or other reference material constitutes plagiarism and may result in disqualification and losing consideration for the job.

Please visit https://www.nasa.gov/careers/how-to-apply/#Artificial-Intelligence to review NASA's guidance on the use of artificial intelligent (AI) or AI-assisted tools during the application process.

Additional information

Additional selections may be made for similar positions across NASA within the local commuting area(s) of the location(s) identified in this announcement . By applying, you agree to have your application shared with interested selecting official(s) within NASA. CTAP/ICTAP will be cleared for any additional selection from this announcement.

For purposes of Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP) selection priority, well-qualified is defined as possessing knowledge, skills, abilities, and/or competencies which clearly exceed the minimum qualification requirements for the position, as determined through SME review of the resume/application. If you have special priority selection rights under ICTAP, you must:

Indicate your eligibility when applying for a position.
Exceed the minimum qualification requirements for the position.
Submit proof that you meet the requirements for ICTAP as indicated in "Required Documents."

For additional information about CTAP/ICTAP eligibility, click here - https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/employee-guide-to-career-transition/#ictap.

Any applicant that received a Voluntary Separation Incentive Payment (VSIP) from the federal governmentwithin the last five years based of the closing date of this announcement, if selected, may be required to repay the full amount prior to establishing a start date. For additional information on the VSIP repayment requirement, click here - https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/voluntary-separation-incentive-payments/.

Per Executive Order 14343, this position is not part of a bargaining unit.

Probationary Period

You may be required to serve a one-year probationary period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. If selected, the requirement to serve such period will be determined by Title 5 of the Code of Federal Regulations, Part 11.

In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider:

your performance and conduct;
the needs and interests of the agency;
whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and
whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service.

Upon completion of your probationary period your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution.

Help

A career with the U.S. government provides employees with a comprehensive benefits package. As a federal employee, you and your family will have access to a range of benefits that are designed to make your federal career very rewarding. Opens in a new windowLearn more about federal benefits.

Review our benefits

Eligibility for benefits depends on the type of position you hold and whether your position is full-time, part-time or intermittent. Contact the hiring agency for more information on the specific benefits offered.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Officer
jobs.description:
Environmental Health Officer

Full-time, fixed-term opportunity until September 2027

Make a visible difference to public health and community wellbeing

$104,790 - $114,015 per annum (pro rata to apply), plus superannuation and RDOs

Commuter-use, tool-of-trade vehicle provided

Help shape a healthier, safer Boroondara. We’re looking for a motivated, community-minded Environmental Health Officer to join our dedicated team and deliver practical, trusted public health outcomes across the municipality.

About the role

You’ll combine fieldwork, investigation and education to protect public health and support local food and health businesses. Working with an experienced team, you’ll conduct inspections, investigate hazards, guide businesses through legislative requirements and take proportionate action where needed. You’ll also participate in a rotating on-call roster, helping our community remain safe, resilient and well informed.

About you

You’re a qualified Environmental Health professional who brings sound knowledge of public health legislation , confident judgement and a genuine commitment to community wellbeing. You communicate clearly, build constructive relationships and approach complex situations with integrity, empathy and practical problem-solving.

You’ll thrive here if you can balance competing priorities, work collaboratively and deliver excellent customer service in a fast - paced regulatory environment. A commitment to continuous learning and improvement will help you make a strong contribution from day one.

Key responsibilities

Undertake inspections, assess compliance and provide clear, practical guidance to food and public health businesses.

Respond to community health complaints and incidents, investigate risks including food adulteration and infectious disease, and take appropriate education or enforcement action.

Maintain accurate records and prepare high-quality reports, notices and evidence for legal proceedings where required.

Represent Council in legal proceedings when required and contribute to health promotion initiatives.

Support the development of colleagues and students, and improve procedures, registers and systems.

Help strengthen public health service delivery and community safety across Boroondara.

Why join us

At the City of Boroondara, your work has a direct and meaningful impact. You’ll join a collaborative, respectful and forward-thinking organisation where people are empowered to contribute ideas, build their capability and deliver better outcomes for the community.

Benefits

Enjoy flexible work arrangements, generous leave entitlements, wellbeing programs , RDOs and ongoing professional development . You’ll be supported by a collaborative team that values your expertise and gives you the opportunity to do work that matters.

If you want to know more about the of working for the City of Boroondara, please visit our

Employment Requirements

Bachelor of Applied Science (Environmental Health) or equivalent including eligibility to be a member of Environmental Health Australia.

Conversant with, and able to interpret, all legislation and standards relating to public health.

Applicants must have the right to work in Australia.

Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check and hold a valid Working with Children Clearance.

How to apply

Ready to make a meaningful contribution to community health? Submit your resume and a cover letter addressing the key selection criteria via the online ‘Apply’ button. Applications close at 11~
59 pm on Friday 16 October 2026.

All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager will be considered. No calls or applications from agencies please.

For any further information please refer to the , or contact Katerina Sioulas - Team Leader Health Services during business hours on 0407 818 480 for a confidential discussion.

We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or to allow us to help in any way we can.

Who are we?

The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals.

We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program.

You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state.

With so much going on it’s a great time to join Boroondara!
